result.note: Tests the AAIB's role and the ICAO interim-statement rule on the AI-171 probe. Skips Air India's commercial troubles, which lack a policy angle.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the investigation into the Air India Flight AI-171 crash of June 2025:
items: In June 2026, an interim statement was issued because International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) rules require one when no final report is issued within twelve months.
The June 2026 interim statement concluded that the crash was caused by a deliberate act.
The preliminary report of July 2025 found that both engine fuel control switches were moved from RUN to CUTOFF soon after take-off.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong. The interim statement declined to name a cause, citing pending international reviews and consultations, and the story says it remains undetermined whether the switch movement was deliberate, accidental or a fault. The probe has reached its final integrated analysis stage.
questions.source: The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) rules require an interim statement when no final report lands within twelve months.

questions.prompt: In June 2026, which body issued an interim statement on its investigation into the crash of Air India Flight AI-171, a Boeing 787-8 flying from Ahmedabad to London?
questions.explain: The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) marked the crash's first anniversary with an interim statement that did not name a cause. The crash on June 12, 2025 left 260 people dead.
questions.source: One year after Air India Flight AI-171, the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau's (AAIB) interim report has still not reached a conclusion on what caused the crash that left 260 people dead.
